chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Sabbah al-Muzani, from al-Harith ibn Husayrah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, who said:
A man met al-Husayn ibn Ali عليه السلام at al-Tha'labiyyah while he was heading toward Karbala. He came to him and greeted him with salām.
So al-Husayn عليه السلام said to him: “From which land are you?” He said: “From the people of al-Kufah.”

He said: “Indeed, by Allah, O brother of the people of al-Kufah, had I met you in al-Madinah, I would have shown you the trace of Jibra'il عليه السلام in our house, and his descent with the revelation upon my grandfather. O brother of the people of al-Kufah, is it that the people drew knowledge from us and then they came to know while we remained ignorant? This is not something that can be.”

key_terms.الثَّعْلَبِيَّةِ: Al-Tha'labiyyah, the location where the encounter took place on the way to Karbala
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: knowledge, especially sacred and authoritative knowledge
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: al-Kufah, the city associated with the man addressed by Imam al-Husayn عليه السلام
key_terms.الْوَحْيِ: divine revelation sent down upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibra'il عليه السلام, the angel who brought revelation
key_terms.دَارِنَا: our house, referring to the household of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.كَرْبَلَاءَ: Karbala, the destination toward which Imam al-Husayn عليه السلام was traveling

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Husayn عليه السلام describe the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام as the source of knowledge?
ai.summary: This narration affirms that the source of divine knowledge after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم remains the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, whose house was the place of revelation. Imam al-Husayn عليه السلام rejects the notion that others could derive knowledge from them while they themselves would be ignorant, underscoring their divinely grounded authority and knowledge.
